Treats the casting function only from the scale/round-trip-fidelity angle (does tier-2 state survive demotion); whether its output is bit-comparable across a language port belongs to the determinism reviewer.
decision_lens: Score P0 when a scheduling, scale, or reconciliation claim (Fork 4's orchestration, Fork 5's scale probe, Decision 9's seamless tier promotion) has no named mechanism or bound at all — the doc's own text admits it isn't solved (e.g. 'still unprobed'), yet other decisions (5, 8) are sequenced as if the answer is already known. Score P1 when a mechanism is named but its fidelity is unverified in the direction that matters most (tier-2-to-tier-1 demotion, not just tier-0-to-tier-1 promotion), or when a budget concept (institutional attention, the tarpit guardrail) is named without being specified as a quantity or rule. Score P2 when a gap is real but doesn't block the current milestone. Score P3 for naming/framing polish.
focus: Whether orchestration inside one app and the LOD reconciliation seam are engineered mechanisms or asserted outcomes — Fork 5's unprobed residents-per-ward/save-size scale hole, Fork 4's unspecified week-tick scheduling trigger, and whether the casting-function identity substrate actually survives round-trips through tier-2 played state in the demotion direction, not just promotion.
name: fd-simarch-lod-orchestration
persona: Apply the perspective of a simulation-at-scale systems architect who has shipped and post-mortemed abstracted-site tick problems in colony-sim and MMO-adjacent engines — someone who has personally watched an unprobed 'residents x wards x save size' axis turn into the thing that blows the performance or storage budget months after ship, and who evaluates every LOD promise ('no visible teleporting,' 'reconciles by construction') by asking what state gets read, written, or discarded at the exact moment of the transition.
review_areas: Fork 5's scale probe as an unpriced dependency — residents-per-observed-ward x observation patterns x save size is named in the doc itself as 'still unprobed,' yet Decision 5 (the LOD ladder) and Decision 8 (one record format) both proceed as settled; assess whether any other decision silently assumes a scale regime that the unprobed axis could invalidate, and whether sequencing epic work (Fork 6) ahead of this probe is defensible or reckless.

Fork 4's orchestration — 'who ticks what when' and 'scheduling street week-ticks against the raven session clock' are named as open questions with no described trigger (wall-clock time? raven-session tick count? player action count? ward-visit events?); assess whether the LOD tier definitions ('the street sim ticks headless at week grain while you play raven mode') actually specify enough to be implementable, or whether 'week grain' is doing unspecified work Fork 4 needs to resolve first.

Tier promotion/demotion fidelity in both directions — Decision 9 asserts entering a ward hands tier-0/1 state up to tier 2 'without visible teleporting' and leaving hands back down, with the casting function `(ward, cohort, slot, seed)` as the identity substrate claimed to survive LOD tiers; assess whether the doc demonstrates (or only asserts by symmetry) that a resident's tier-2 played-state richness — arcs, ties, being-Seen history — actually round-trips into tier-1's coarser headless representation on exit without silent loss, and whether that lossiness is compatible with the engramicon `lossiness` field the doc cites as evidence of fit.

The institutional-attention budget (the tarpit guardrail on the upward channel) — arc → episode → effect table → drift → crystallization is 'budgeted by institutional attention'; assess whether this budget is specified anywhere as a quantity, formula, refill rate, or cap, or whether it functions as a placeholder name for 'we will rate-limit this somehow,' leaving the upward channel's core safety property unenforced.

Tier-0 'reconciles by construction' under Tier-1 runtime mutation — assess whether Tier 0's construction-time reconciliation against `households_total` is preserved once Tier 1 wards begin feeding headless week-tick state back into the aggregate layer, or whether the aggregates-authoritative invariant (held fixed for this review) needs an explicit runtime reconciliation check rather than relying on the construction-time guarantee alone.

Check against the predecessor melange's still-binding scale/reconciliation findings (2026-08-11 synthesis, e.g. household reconciliation f-031, the JIA/population-0 carve-out f-033) for whether the one-game frame's orchestration/scheduling moves silently under-specify any of them — in particular whether Fork 2's 'reconciliation invariant... realization rules for every aggregate flow' was more fully specified in the predecessor design than it is here, and if so, what got dropped in the rewrite.

severity_examples.condition: No numeric, formulaic, or rate-based specification exists for institutional attention anywhere in the document or its referenced canon.
